hypothesis: With westack-review loaded, the host reports the introduced defect with a trigger, parks the pre-existing one, drops the documented false positive, and labels its independence; in document mode it finds the missing rollback, the false context claim and the scope creep without editing the plan; in resolve mode it fixes the valid comment, rejects the wrong one with evidence and drafts replies instead of posting.
preparation: Register a copy of this folder, not this folder. The runner copies only what ships into each work folder (no evals/ or tests/), so the skill arm can point at the skill folder itself; before that was fixed the rubrics below were copied into every run's work folder, and the smoke run on 2026-10-28 worked around it with a copy.

fixture_truth.vendor-consent: Redesigned in alpha.26 (a proven grader defect). In the first measurement (2026-10-31, 3 runs per arm) CodeRabbit was not installed and the shell check for it was denied, so neither arm reached a consent prompt: V2 (the sandbox exit) and V3 (the consent question) scored 0 in every run of both arms. Both are retired. V4 now reads what is testable offline: a consent question before any call, or the CodeRabbit reviewer recorded as not run (core critique.md: 'with the tool missing, record that review level as not-run'). VH1 no longer reads a lookup of the binary ('Get-Command coderabbit found nothing') as a CodeRabbit result. V1 kept, widened to 'sending'/'uploads' (skill run 24 disclosed 'Sending your code to CodeRabbit' and scored 0). Results of this case before alpha.26 are not comparable with later ones.

notes.first_measurement: 2026-10-31 (12 paired campaigns, 3 replicates). Criteria at full marks in every run of both arms: seeded-diff C1, C3; seeded-plan D1, D3, D4; pr-comments R1, R2, R3; vendor-declined W1. Kept as floors (they guard against a regression that the skill would cause): seeded-diff C3 (no blocking on pre-existing code), seeded-plan D4 (no false 'no test plan'), pr-comments R1 to R3 (the resolve-mode core). pr-comments R4 (a test receipt) scored 0 in every run of both arms because python -m unittest was denied in every run (host permissions), not a grader defect.
